gaps.quote: Let $b$ be the bit length of $n,$
gaps.note: Inconsistent with the next definition b=ceil(log2 n): the bit length of n is floor(log2 n)+1, which differs from ceil(log2 n) when n is a power of two. The paper (line 4055) defines b=ceil(log_2 n).

The page does not derive b/2 <= log2 T <= b from the range of T and n, and the ell upper bound p/(3d) also needs d <= b and the ceiling in r; these hypotheses (paper lines 4074-4076) are not stated, so the reader cannot check the constants 1/12, 1, 1/3.

gaps.quote: The deterministic search for the primes takes $n^{o(1)}=o(n)$ time
gaps.note: The page never describes the search or its cost (the paper, lines 4160-4171, scans the intervals with trial division, giving O(d r^{3/2} poly(p)) time); the claim that its logarithm is o(p) cannot be checked from the page.
